mechanism_narrative: The continued week-to-week recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals more commuting and downtown trip chaining, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as weekday discretionary stops expand.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising over the next month but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS after the winter peak indicates substitution away from outdoor leisure toward enclosed shopping and dining, which should raise RETAIL_REC within two weeks as recreation demand reallocates indoors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 10 points week-on-week from an already depressed level
failure_condition: If PARKS falls further or stays weak but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain elevated together, households are staying local and making more short neighborhood trips, which can spill over into nearby retail visits and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays near or above baseline while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in WORKPLACES below the recent trend would indicate renewed tightening or compliance pressure, reducing discretionary shopping trips and pushing RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops by more than 2 points week-on-week after a four-week recovery
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES falls sharply but RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days, the policy-sensitive demand channel is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover together, commuting confidence rises and people are more likely to combine errands with work travel, producing a higher RETAIL_REC level over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue improving but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 28 days, the commuting-spillover hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rebound in PARKS from very depressed winter levels marks improving weather and outdoor activity, which should also support retail trips after a short lag as people extend outings into commercial areas.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points from the prior week after being below -30
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds materially but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, the weather-linked retail lift is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL implies more people are moving around while still spending time near home, which should generate neighborhood retail demand and lift RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 to 14 days, the neighborhood-demand interaction is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps moving toward baseline while PARKS stays well below baseline, consumers are shifting from necessary trips and outdoor leisure toward discretionary indoor shopping, which should raise RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5 while PARKS remains below -20
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM improves and PARKS stays depressed but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its previous 28-day mean, the mechanism is rejected.
